source_version.title: The additive indecomposability of the primes

common_hypothesis.statement: After finite-factor reduction, fixed infinite A,B subsets of nonnegative integers have finite symmetric difference between A+B and the positive primes; both eventual prime coverage and eventual exclusion of composite sums are assumed.
common_hypothesis.partitions: D=-B; choose S_p and its complement containing respectively the A and D residues beyond p+N_*; 0<sigma_p<1.
common_hypothesis.norm_warning: Collision uses counting L2 of probability masses; finite-field function norms use probability measure.
common_hypothesis.quantifier_warning: Large depth and gap parameters are fixed before L tends to infinity.

claims.exact_scope: For every A,B subset N_0 with at least two elements each, (A+B) symmetric-difference P is infinite.
claims.missing_obligation: Establish the two-infinite-set arithmetic contradiction, not merely a finite-field lemma.

claims.exact_scope: Eventual decomposition with both summands of cardinality at least two implies both summands infinite.
dependencies: additive large sieve and Mertens in the fixed-shift proof
claims.missing_obligation: An independent arithmetic certification would still need the fixed-shift sieve and its classical estimates; old local work did not supply it.

claims.exact_scope: No infinite A,B subset N_0 have (A+B) symmetric-difference P finite.
dependencies: complete arithmetic construction and its antecedents
claims.missing_obligation: Verify the global arithmetic chain through the final contradiction.

claims.exact_scope: For fixed b>=1, probability measures on the stated opposite tails, maximal atom <= (log X)^b/sqrt(X), and Q=sqrt(X)/(log X)^(b+1), the nonnegative log-p-weighted sum of two counting-L2 stability errors plus the complementary-density defect is O_b(log log X).
dependencies: size lemma for uniform long-tail applications
claims.missing_obligation: For every application verify tail support, maximal atom, cutoff and counting-norm normalization; do not extend to unrestricted measures.

claims.exact_scope: Under the common decomposition hypothesis, the log-p/p-weighted maximal translated quadratic bias on T<=log p<=2T is o(T); centers vary independently with p. Every fixed positive log-log band has harmonic bias sum o(L_*).
dependencies: uniform amplified moment and Poisson argument
claims.missing_obligation: Audit the independently varying-center argument, coefficient-array uniformity, kernel count and exceptional-character split-prime estimate at source lines 113-1058.

claims.exact_scope: For every fixed 0<alpha<beta, the 1/p-weighted sum on alpha L<=log log p<=beta L of maximal translated bias over all multiplicative characters of order >2 is o(L). Character and center may vary with p.
claims.not_a_load_bearing_dependency_of_this_pr: C_QUADRATIC; it is needed in the subsequent mixed-flatness corollary instead
claims.missing_obligation: Audit uniformity over unbounded character order, anchor cancellation, diagonals and final comparison at source lines 348-1115.

claims.exact_scope: For every fixed 0<alpha<beta, outside harmonic prime mass o(L) in that log-log band, sigma_p=1/2+o(1) and the maximum mixed additive-multiplicative correlation of the exact centered normalized transform g_p is o(1), uniformly; principal characters are included and zero at zero.
dependencies: exact inversion for the principal character
claims.missing_obligation: Establish both translated decorrelation inputs and retain the correct harmonic exceptional-set quantifier, rather than asserting all-prime flatness.

claims.exact_scope: An absolute delta_0>0 gives harmonic mass at least .15L for every sufficiently large L among primes with .05L<=log log p<=.9L, 1/3<=sigma_p<=2/3 and E|g_p|>=delta_0.
dependencies: classical total primitive-character prime-error estimate with exceptional deletion
coverage of every sufficiently large prime
claims.missing_obligation: Verify the tensor upper bound and the weighted full-prime lower bound, including unweighted character-error summation and exceptional-conductor deletion.

claims.exact_scope: At fixed construction constants and sufficiently large fixed k before L->infinity, eq:src55 holds uniformly in either specified final or diagonal environment. Eq:src56 additionally requires l>=2 and <=3r/4 overlap components; its exponent omega_k(m)/m tends to infinity. All support, giant-frequency unit tests and the specified couplings are hypotheses.
dependencies: C_TREE as a separately assessed per-prime input
claims.missing_obligation: Justify replacement of actual coupled arithmetic histories by the exact Haar-unit component-product law with uniform negligible errors before applying the tree theorem, and independently control the norm frequency sums.

claims.exact_scope: Under the stated hierarchy, initial |eta_0|>=exp(-B_*m), exact transfer split and diagonal reserve imply |eta_j|>=exp(-c_g)|eta_(j-1)|^2/2 and -log|eta_j|<=2^j B_*m+(2^j-1)(c_g+log 2)<B 2^j m; at r=2^k this gives |eta_k|^2>=exp(-2B r m).
dependencies: positive statistic and initial Poisson bound
C_ARITH and bad-arrangement count for the diagonal reserve
claims.missing_obligation: Establish the initial arithmetic lower bound, exact diagonal split and uniform diagonal bound; the scalar iteration alone supplies none of them.

claims.exact_scope: After the gap constants choose sufficiently large fixed k with r=2^k and z=k^4, then large L. Permutation symmetrization, the comparison bounds and the regular-factor norm imply |eta_k|^2<=exp(-(2B+1)r m), contradicting C_TRANSFER.
dependencies: fixed-k frequency budget and superexponential comparison decay
claims.missing_obligation: Verify the separate actual-prime regular-factor norm at 09:205-306 and the uniform arithmetic comparisons; local tree/algebra certificates do not certify them.

checked_compatibility: a(x)b(x)=x/log x, compatible with the asymptotic coverage lower bound and O(x) product upper bound
for every fixed positive integer j, a(x),b(x)=o(x/(log x)^j) and exceed every fixed polylogarithmic lower bound
the sharper Elsholtz-Harper growth bounds quoted in the introduction also permit this scale
retired_route.exact_count_caveat: The literal model is checked against the listed asymptotic product restriction, not A(x)B(x)>=pi(x)-O(1); a fixed constant enlargement would preserve all the listed growth compatibilities.
